29182.description:
Program Manager, MCH


Reports to:       
Country Director


Location:          
Port Moresby (up to 20% Provincial Travel)


Background


The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low- and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.


CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work in conjunction with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.


At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skillsets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: 
http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org


CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds and culture.


Program Overview


CHAI has been supporting the Ministry of Health in PNG since 2005, working across HIV, immunization, malaria, nutrition, non-communicable diseases (NCDs), and broader health system strengthening. This long-standing partnership reflects CHAI’s commitment to sustainable, government-led health system improvements in PNG.


CHAI’s support for the MCH program began in 2019 and has focused primarily on immunization and nutrition. Over the past six years, CHAI has worked closely with the Government of PNG to set program priorities and drive strategic improvements. Key achievements include spearheading the development of the National Immunisation Strategy, supporting the government to conduct a comprehensive zero-dose analysis, and providing instrumental technical and programmatic support in close collaboration with government and other partners.


PNG continues to face significant maternal and child health challenges, including uneven immunization coverage, difficult service delivery contexts, and constrained sub-national capacity. As the Government of PNG implements its National Immunisation Strategy and prepares for the introduction of new vaccines while strengthening routine immunization and primary health care, CHAI is expanding its support at both national and provincial levels. This includes providing hands-on implementation support in select provinces, strengthening government planning and coordination systems, and building sustainable capacity for improved MCH service delivery.


Position Summary


CHAI is seeking a Program Manager for MCH to provide leadership for CHAI’s MCH cluster in PNG, covering the Immunization and Nutrition programs. This role will provide strategic leadership, technical oversight, and project management for the cluster.


The ideal candidate is a credible program leader who excels at managing high-performing teams, overseeing grant implementation and nurturing deep trusted relationships with government partners. We are specifically seeking a candidate with strong monitoring and evaluation capabilities, technical capabilities and exceptional project management skills. The position requires someone who can engage confidently with senior government counterparts, lead complex vaccine and immunization workstreams, and support effective implementation at provincial level.


Reporting to the Country Director, the Program Manager will have day-to-day leadership responsibility for CHAI’s MCH portfolio and will be responsible for growing it. The Program Manager will directly set and manage the program workplan, manage the budget, monitor performance and report to donors, and manage relationships with government and donors. The role requires balancing strategic thinking with hands-on program management, ensuring strong execution while also shaping the future direction and growth of CHAI’s MCH work in PNG.


Performance in this role is reviewed monthly against the role’s accountability scorecard.


Key Responsibilities




Serve as CHAI’s primary day-to-day counterpart to the National EPI Program and National Nutrition Program within the National Department of Health, keeping the engagement log current and holding a weekly HPV and AIHSS huddle.


Build and maintain strong, respectful working relationships with senior government officials, Provincial Health Authorities and key partners.


Represent CHAI in national and sub-national technical working groups, coordination forums and joint reviews.


Provide leadership, mentoring and support to the MCH team, ensuring staff receive timely guidance and support to address challenges, with issues escalated when necessary. Foster a supportive team culture grounded in accountability and learning.


Oversee the program budget, monitor utilization, flag potential over- and underspends early, and ensure program requests are reviewed and approved promptly.


Ensure high-quality program delivery in line with donor commitments, manage donor relationships, and lead the development of concept notes and proposals as the portfolio evolves.


Lead the planning, implementation and monitoring of CHAI’s MCH workplan, including annual operational plans and Nutrition and AIHSS deliverables, ensuring alignment with government priorities and drawing on CHAI’s global technical expertise where relevant.


Provide hands-on management of CHAI’s support to routine immunization service delivery, including outreach, supervision and performance improvement at provincial level.


Lead CHAI’s technical and programmatic support for new vaccine introductions, including the introduction roadmap, readiness planning, coordination and implementation.


Support the Government of PNG to operationalize and roll out the National Immunization Strategy, translating national priorities into practical implementation plans.


Oversee CHAI’s support to the National Nutrition Program, ensuring effective coordination and implementation, including timely payment of village health assistants and regular supportive supervision.


Work closely with the Country Director to translate strategic direction into practical workplans and measurable results.


Contribute to shaping the future direction and growth of CHAI’s MCH portfolio by identifying emerging priorities, gaps and opportunities for impact, in line with CHAI’s regional and global strategies.


Identify implementation risks and operational challenges and develop practical mitigation measures.


Ensure program data is used effectively to inform decision-making, monitor progress and guide course correction.


Lead the preparation of clear, high-quality reports and updates for government counterparts, donors and CHAI leadership, including a one-page monthly report to the Country Director.


Share key lessons and risks from PNG with regional and global counterparts to inform CHAI’s broader strategy and learning.


Support other organization-wide priorities as assigned by the Country Director.


Uphold CHAI’s values and standards of professionalism and accountability and contribute to internal leadership initiatives and cross-team problem-solving.




Qualifications




Master’s degree in public health, health sciences, or a health-related field.


Minimum of 7 years of relevant professional experience in public health or development, with demonstrated responsibility for program leadership and delivery.


Strong experience in vaccines and immunization, including service delivery and new vaccine introduction; nutrition experience is an asset.


Strong monitoring and evaluation skills, including experience designing M&E frameworks, analyzing program data, and using evidence to drive program improvements.


Demonstrated excellence in stakeholder management and relationship-building, particularly with government partners in complex, multi-stakeholder environments.


Proven experience working closely with government counterparts in low-resource or complex settings.


Demonstrated ability to lead teams, manage multiple workstreams, and support field-based implementation, including managing managers and provincial teams.


Strong financial and grant management skills, including managing a donor-funded portfolio against clear performance measures and raising risks early.


Strong judgment, maturity, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to earn credibility and trust with senior stakeholders.


Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

[email protected]


Application Deadline:
 30 November 2026


 





            

        
Apply

High Voltage Technician


Master Systems Technologies (MST) is seeking a qualified and motivated High Voltage Technician to join our growing operations/engineering team.


Key Responsibilities




Perform installation, testing, commissioning, maintenance, and troubleshooting of High Voltage (HV) and Low Voltage (LV) electrical systems.


Carry out HV switching, isolation, and safety procedures in accordance with industry standards.


Maintain and fault-find transformers, switchgear, protection relays, circuit breakers, generators, and distribution networks.


Conduct preventative and corrective maintenance on electrical infrastructure.


Prepare maintenance reports, test records, and commissioning documentation.


Ensure all work is completed safely and in compliance with company and regulatory requirements.




Requirements




Recognized Electrical Trade Qualification.


High Voltage Switching Certification.


Minimum 3-5 years' experience working with HV and LV electrical systems.


Strong knowledge of power generation, electrical distribution, switchgear, transformers, and protection systems.


Ability to read and interpret electrical drawings and schematics.


Current Driver's Licence.


Mining, industrial, or power station experience will be highly regarded.




Desired Attributes




Strong commitment to workplace safety.


Excellent troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.


Ability to work independently and as part of a team.


Willingness to travel and work on remote project sites as required.

:




Updated CV


Copies of relevant qualifications and trade certificates


Contactable references




Please note that shortlisted candidates will be required to undergo a

 before employment.

Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


As K92 continues expanding our underground gold mine near Kainantu, safety remains our number one priority, as such, we seek to add an additional Senior Safety Officer to the team who will be responsible for ensuring that all safety regulations and procedures are followed at our Kainantu Gold Mine. This role is a crucial role in preventing accidents and incidents, protecting the health and safety of employees, contractors and maintaining compliance with Papua New Guinea’s safety laws and regulations.


Key Accountabilities




Ensuring the continuous improvement of, safety inspections, safety training and compliance.


Maintain a safe work environment for all K92 employees, visitors and contractors through audits, inspections, and training.


Maintain the efficiency and cost-effective management of safety in the workplace and project site.


Ensure all incidents are fully investigated and recorded within the site safety data base in a timely and accurate manner.


Development of safety training programs and initiatives.


Develop scheduled, weekly, monthly safety audits and checks project wide


Collate and submit weekly and monthly reports to Project Director and Operational GM.


Attend site wide weekly and monthly safety meetings.


Ensuring that the camp and project sites safety regulations are observed by all K92 employees including contractors,


Provide safety induction to new intakes, casuals, contractors, and visitors to site.


To ensure the safety rules and other policies of the camp and mine site are observed and report any suspicious activities




About You 


To be considered for this role, you must have a Degree or Diploma in Health & Safety/Environmental Health from a recognized institution or equivalent., in addition you must have some or all of the following




At least 10 years’ experience in occupational health and safety in mining environment would be an advantage A Diploma or certificate in Health Extension or General Nursing is an advantage.


Current PNG Driver’s license.


Training and Assessment experience and qualifications.


Possess good training skills


Completion of accredited fire training.


Current first aid certificate.


Well-versed experience in project safety management.


Excellent oral and written communication skills.


Proficient in computer and e-mail correspondences.


Ability to meet communicated schedules and deadlines.


Strong planning, interpersonal and organizational skills


Exposure to Emergency Response teams, processes.




Life at K92  


K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.


In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster. 


THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

Summary


BCM) Coordinator sits between the BCM Officers and the Team Leader — translating strategy into structured, well-managed delivery. This role is required to move beyond just producing content and is ready to own projects, manage timelines, support the team, and ensure the quality of everything that goes out under the Glory Group name. The coordination 
works across multiple business functions simultaneously — property development, construction, food and beverage, education, community engagement, and non-profit programs — and act as the first point of guidance for BCM Officers.


Duties and Responsibilities


Project & Campaign Coordination


–    Coordinate BCM campaigns and projects across all business functions — from brief to delivery — ensuring work is planned, assigned, tracked, and completed on time.


–    Develop and maintain content calendars, project timelines, and delivery schedules across property development, real estate, construction, food and beverage, education, community, and non-profit programs.


–    Brief BCM Officers on tasks clearly and in detail — setting expectations, timelines, and quality standards upfront so work is executed correctly the first time.


–    Track progress across all active workstreams and proactively flag risks, delays, or resource issues to the Team Leader.


–    Manage the BCM team's shared task and project management tools, keeping records current and accessible.


Content Oversight & Quality Control


–    Review and approve all content produced by BCM Officers before it is published, submitted, or presented — checking for brand consistency, accuracy, tone, and quality.


–    Provide clear, constructive feedback to Officers to help them improve and meet the team's standards.


–    Contribute directly to the production of high-priority, complex, or sensitive content pieces as required.


–    Maintain and update the company's content library, asset management system, and brand guidelines documentation.


–    Ensure that content produced across all business functions — property, food and beverage, education, community, non-profit — is cohesive and on-brand.


Stakeholder & Departmental Liaison


–    Serve as the day-to-day point of contact between the BCM team and internal departments including property development, construction, food and beverage, education, community engagement, and non-profit operations.


–    Gather project briefs from departments, clarify requirements, and communicate realistic timelines and deliverables.


–    Build and maintain strong working relationships across all functions so BCM is seen as a trusted, responsive partner.


–    Liaise with external vendors, suppliers, photographers, printers, and partners as required for campaigns and events.


Events Coordination


–    Lead the planning and coordination of company events across all business functions — property launches, food and beverage activations, school open days, community programs, and non-profit initiatives.


–    Develop event runsheets, manage vendor relationships, coordinate logistics, and oversee on-the-day execution with the support of BCM Officers.


–    Ensure all events are well-documented through photography, video, and written coverage, and that content is captured and used effectively post-event.


–    Prepare post-event reports and ensure learnings are applied to future activations.


Reporting & Team Administration


–    Prepare regular written updates and progress reports on BCM activities for the Team Leader and BCM Lead.


–    Monitor and compile social media and campaign performance data, and contribute insights to strategy discussions.


–    Maintain organised team records, filing systems, and documentation so information is easy to find and use.


–    Support the onboarding of new BCM team members by familiarising them with systems, processes, and standards.


Job Requirements


–    Bachelor's Degree in Communications, Marketing, Media, Business, or a related field.

29168.description:
Legal Policy Support Adviser – Strongim Wok Long TVET


 




Fixed term contract up to December 2027 (with possible extension)


Based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea


Open to PNG and International candidates


Up to 100 input days, remote and in-country




 


About Palladium


Palladium is a global leader in the design, development, and delivery of Positive Impact – the intentional creation of enduring social and economic value.  We work with governments, businesses, and investors to solve the world's most pressing challenges. With a team of more than 2,000 employees operating in 75-plus countries and a global network of over 35,000 experts, we help improve economies, societies, and, most importantly, people's lives.
 


About PNG-Australia Strongim Wok Long TVET (SWLT)


The PNG–Australia Strongim Wok Long Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) (SWLT) program is a four-year, AUD 80 million investment by the Australian Government Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to support Papua New Guinea’s (PNG) efforts to strengthen its TVET sector. Aligned with PNG’s national priority to build an educated and skilled workforce for resilient economic growth, SWLT aims to enhance the quality, relevance, and inclusiveness of skills development. The program supports improvements in national quality assurance systems, technical college standards, graduate employability, and Australia’s visible and trusted development partnership with PNG.


The program aligns with the broader goals of the 
Australia–PNG Development Partnership Plan 2024–2029
, which emphasises locally led development, education investment, and inclusive growth, as well as 
PNG’s Higher and Technical Education Reform Act 2020
.


This Opportunity


As 
Legal Policy Support Adviser, 
you will provide development support to PNG’s Department of Higher Education, Research, Science, and Technology (DHERST) legal staff to strengthen individual and institutional capacity to fulfil their legislated functions and lead priority higher education and TVET reforms.


You will provide capacity building support to DHERST counterparts to assist with the implementation of priority reform initiatives. The role will improve DHERST’s capacity and capability to undertake policy development, legislative reform, regulatory oversight and service delivery, while strengthening institutional systems and processes required to implement and sustain reform outcomes in line with Government of Papua New Guinea (GoPNG) and DHERST legislative, policies, strategies and plans.


Primary Responsibilities


The activity will comprise of but not be limited to the following:


Policy, Legislative and Regulatory Reform




Work with DHERST counterparts to strengthen legal and regulatory capability in support of higher and technical education reforms.


Support DHERST counterparts to interpret, apply, and implement legislative, regulatory, and policy reforms, and identify practical solutions to reform barriers.


Work with DHERST counterparts, including the Quality Assurance Division, to strengthen regulatory processes and oversight of higher and technical education institutions.


Develop practical tools, templates, guidance materials, and procedures with DHERST counterparts to support legal, regulatory, and compliance functions.


Review legal and regulatory processes with DHERST counterparts and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, consistency, and compliance.


Support DHERST counterparts to implement regulatory oversight functions across universities, technical institutions, and other tertiary education providers.




Stakeholder Engagement




Support counterparts in advocacy and negotiation processes associated with reform initiatives.


Collaborate with counterparts on stakeholder communications and engagement approaches.


Support counterparts to develop tools and approaches for consultations with government agencies, institutions and industry stakeholders.




Capacity Strengt
hening




Work closely with DHERST counterparts to build legal and regulatory capability through mentoring, coaching, on-the-job training, and knowledge transfer.


Support DHERST counterparts to strengthen their skills in legal research, legislative interpretation, regulatory implementation, compliance monitoring, and stakeholder engagement.


Work with DHERST counterparts to develop practical tools, guidance materials, and documented processes that support sustainable legal and regulatory functions.


Facilitate stakeholder engagement and consultation activities with DHERST counterparts to support legal and regulatory implementation.


Monitor capability development progress with DHERST counterparts, incorporating feedback and lessons learned to strengthen long-term institutional capability.


Support DHERST counterparts to undertake planning, monitoring, reporting, and learning activities in line with SWLT and DHERST priorities.


Participate in self-reflection, feedback and pulse-check activities to monitor the effectiveness of the capability strengthening approach and adjust support in response to feedback.




Coordination and Integration




Work closely with DHERST counterparts, SWLT team members and other related activities to ensure approaches are coherent and complementary, including participation in scheduled coordination meetings within SWLT, DHERST and DFAT.


Support alignment between MEL, planning, budgeting, reporting, reform implementation and digital systems development where relevant.




Cross-cutting Priorities




Ensure advice, support and review processes consider and address a) gender equality, b) disability and c) social inclusion, locally led development, child protection and PSEAH safeguarding, sustainability and other SWLT cross-cutting priorities.


Support the collection and use of disaggregated data where practical and appropriate, including data relevant to gender, disability, youth, location and other priority groups.


Ensure proposed systems, tools and reporting processes are practical, ethical, inclusive and aligned with SWLT and DHERST requirements.




General SWLT 




Contribute to the development and implementation of solutions that deliver value and ensure SWLT principles
[1]
 are embedded within program delivery.


Comply with all safeguarding, including child protection and PSEAH requirements, and promptly report any safeguarding concerns in accordance with SWLT and Palladium policies and procedures.


Support and uphold the organisation’s commitment to environmental sustainability, such as reducing resource use and promoting climate-friendly practices.




 


About you


You will demonstrate proven experience in the following areas:


Technical Skills and Experience




Minimum seven years' experience providing legal, legislative, regulatory and/or legal policy advice.


Demonstrated experience in mentoring, skills transfer and institutional capacity development, including supporting counterparts to strengthen legal, policy and regulatory capability.


Significant experience supporting legislative reviews, policy reform processes and the development of legal and regulatory frameworks, preferably within the public sector, higher education, TVET or related sectors.


Demonstrated experience working with senior government officials and executive decision-makers.


Strong legal research, policy analysis and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate complex legal concepts into practical and accessible guidance for a range of audiences.


Excellent drafting skills, including experience preparing legislation, regulations, policy papers, briefs, reports and other technical or knowledge products.


Demonstrated understanding of government legislative and policy processes, within Papua New Guinea or a comparable context.


Experience working with, or knowledge of, the higher education and/or TVET sector, including relevant legislative, policy and institutional arrangements.


Proven ability to facilitate consultations, manage stakeholder relationships and build consensus among diverse groups.




Personal Attributes




Excellent interpersonal, communication and cross-cultural engagement skills, with the ability to work effectively with government, development partners and other stakeholders.


Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively, adapt to changing priorities and deliver high-quality outputs within agreed timeframes.


Knowledge of the international development sector and an interest in supporting sustainable institutional strengthening and reform.


Demonstrated commitment to environmental and social safeguards and the integration of gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) principles and commitments in program delivery and capacity development activities.




To Apply


Please submit your application online, including your CV and brief cover letter, outlining your suitability in line with the requirements of the position through 
https://palladium.csod.com/ux/ats/careersite/2/home/requisition/25737?c=palladium


Closing date: 
Friday 20
th
 November 2026, 5.00pm AEST


Equity, Diversity & Inclusion -
 Palladium is committed to embedding equity, diversity, and inclusion into everything we do. We welcome applications from all sections of society and actively encourage diversity to drive innovation, creativity, success and good practice. We positively welcome and seek to ensure we achieve diversity in our workforce; and that all job applicants and employees receive equal and fair treatment regardless of their background or personal characteristics. These include: (but are not limited to) socio-economic background, age, race, gender identity and expression, religion, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, nationality, veteran, marital or Indigenous status.


Should you require any adjustments to be made due to a disability or you are a neurodivergent individual or for any other circumstance, please email our team at 
[email protected]
 and we will be in touch to discuss.


Safeguarding -
 We define Safeguarding as “the preventative action taken by Palladium to protect our people, clients and the communities we work with from harm”. We are committed to ensuring that all children and adults who come into contact with Palladium are treated with respect and are free from abuse. All successful candidates will be subject to an enhanced selection process including safeguarding-focused interviews and a rigorous due diligence process.





    	        
Apply

29167.description:
Senior Lecturer - Business Statistics, Data Analytics & Mathematics


School of Business & Management (SoBM) - Port Moresby, NCD




 












 


Position title: Lecturer/Senior Lecturer – Business Statistics, Data Analytics & Mathematics


School: School of Business & Management (SoBM)


Location: IBSUniversity, 11 Mile Campus, Port Moresby


Reports to: Head – School of Business & Management


Employment type: Full-time


 


IBSUniversity seeks a full-time Lecturer/Senior Lecturer to teach Business Statistics, Data Analytics and Mathematics within the School of Business & Management (SoBM), working under the Head of School.


 


About the Role


The Lecturer is the gatekeeper of student success, helping students gain the quantitative and analytical skills they need to prosper in business careers. This role delivers the school’s quantitative stream: Business Statistics, Data Analytics and Mathematics for undergraduate and graduate programs.


 


The Lecturer will use digital tools and real business data to deliver an engaging learning experience, keep students engaged academically and socially, and make effective use of the University's finite academic resources. The role involves a high degree of unsupervised work. We are looking for an outcome-focused person with strong conflict-resolution skills who manages their own workload well and works productively in a team.


 


Key Responsibilities


The Lecturer will teach and develop undergraduate units in Business Statistics, Data Analytics and Mathematics, and will manage and monitor associated programs, including operational administration, curriculum development, course materials review and quality enhancement. Duties include, but are not limited to, the following.


 


Learning & Teaching




Teach Business Statistics, Data Analytics and Mathematics for undergraduate and graduate programs.


Deliver lectures, tutorials and computer-lab sessions to individuals and groups and complete the assigned syllabus within the scheduled time.


Use statistical and analytics software and other teaching aids to improve understanding and delivery.


Use real business and local industry datasets so that students apply quantitative methods to practical decisions.


Monitor student attendance and progress and achieve the benchmark set in the semester KPIs.


Use the Institution's pre-determined resources to deliver teaching as outlined.


 




Lesson Preparation, Assessment & Examination




Design, prepare and conduct face-to-face, online and cooperative learning sessions that inspire discussion and keep students engaged.


Ensure unit design and delivery comply with the quality standards and regulations of the University and College.


Set assessments, mark and moderate, supervise and invigilate examinations.


Prepare and submit DRMS on time.




Student Learning Experience




Provide a high-quality learning experience that helps students achieve the prescribed learning outcomes, including support for students who find mathematics and statistics difficult.


Supervise student projects, including data-driven research projects, and the academic elements of field trips as required.


Support students' extracurricular activities.


Coordinate meetings and schedules with tutees.




Curriculum Development




Develop and produce learning materials, datasets, lab exercises and assessment methods of the highest quality for undergraduate programs.


Design and deliver modules and curriculum and review them regularly to keep them current with industry practice and analytics tools.


Work with other schools to embed quantitative and data skills across programs.




Research, Scholarship & Innovation




Research and publication record in quantitative or applied business areas.


Engage in research, scholarly activity and innovation, subject to the approval of the Head of School.


Work with researchers internally, nationally and internationally to contribute to the research objectives of the School and the Institution's research centers.


Maintain subject and professional development relevant to teaching and contribute actively to the subject association and relevant professional bodies.




General Duties




Attend and present at relevant conferences, and share insights with other schools when required.


Liaise closely with teaching, technical and administration staff.


Take on administrative responsibilities as requested by the Head of School


Take part in professional development and staff development initiatives on learning and teaching and continue to grow cultural competence.


Support the team in other operational activities as required.




Key Selection Criteria


Essential




Master's degree or higher in Statistics, Mathematics, Data Science/Analytics, Applied Mathematics, Economics/Econometrics or a closely related quantitative field. A Business degree with a strong quantitative major may be considered.


At least 3 years' experience teaching statistics, mathematics or data analytics at tertiary level.


Demonstrated ability to teach quantitative subjects to business students, including those with limited mathematical background.


Proficiency in at least one statistical or analytics tool (Excel, SPSS, R, Python, Power BI or Tableau) and the ability to teach it.


Well-developed interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with students and with employees and management at all levels.


Excellent analytical, business-judgement and decision-making skills.


Ability to review programme design regularly to ensure compliance with quality standards and academic regulations, and to make changes where appropriate.


Ability to use a range of delivery techniques to enthuse and engage students.


Ability to develop and maintain effective working relationships with students, staff, management, other organizations and external stakeholders.


Ability to explain complex quantitative ideas in several ways: presentations, reports, journal articles and so on.


Ability to plan workloads and projects and manage resources effectively.


Sound computer skills.




Desirable




PhD in a relevant field.


Experience teaching in a business school or with business and management programs.


Experience with learning management systems and online or blended delivery.


Industry or consulting experience in data analysis, research or business intelligence.


Knowledge of Papua New Guinea's business environment and local data sources.













    	        
Apply

We are currently seeking a suitably skilled and experienced Occupational Health & Safety (OHS) Officer to join our Human Capital Team to maintain and improve health, safety and wellbeing practices, procedures and policies across the Company.


 


ABOUT THE ROLE


 


Reporting to the Team Leader – Training & Development, the OHS Officer ensures a safe, healthy, and compliant workplace. The role involves developing and implementing safety procedures, conducting risk assessments, leading safety training, investigating incidents, and supporting a strong safety culture.


 


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


 




Develop and update OHS policies and procedures.


Communicate safety requirements and ensure compliance across the organisation.


Conduct safety audits and risk assessments to identify hazards.


Implement corrective actions to reduce risks.


Investigate incidents and maintain accurate records.


Deliver safety training, inductions, and refresher sessions.


Ensure compliance with OHS legislation and industry standards.


Liaise with regulatory bodies during audits and inspections.


Develop and test emergency response and evacuation plans.


Coordinate emergency drills and response teams.


Support health and wellness programs, ergonomic assessments, and awareness activities.


Maintain inventory of safety equipment and Personal Protective Equipment.


Analyse safety data and identify improvement strategies and opportunities.




 


REQUIREMENTS


 




Bachelor’s degree or Diploma in HR, Business, Environment, Science, or related field.


OHS certification is an advantage.


Minimum 3 years’ experience in OHS or a related safety role.


Strong knowledge of OHS laws, including PNG Labour Laws and the Employment Act.


Experience in safety audits, incident reporting, and risk assessments.


Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.


Excellent communication and training abilities.


Ability to remain calm under pressure and make sound decisions.


High attention to detail and commitment to safety.




 


HOW TO APPLY


 


If you are passionate about pursuing a career with Moni Plus and enjoy being part of a high-performing team, we’d love to hear from you. Please submit your resume and a cover letter outlining your relevant experience and why you are the ideal candidate for this position.

Please note only shortlisted applicants will be contacted to proceed.

13th November 2026.

29162.description:
Summary






The selected candidate will oversee all accounting operations, including accounts payable, receivable, and financial reporting. This role involves managing a team of accountants to ensure accurate recording of financial transactions, compliance with tax regulations, and preparation of audit materials. S/he will specifically focus on accounting functions and collaborate with the Finance Department on related financial planning and analysis activities.


Duties and Responsibilities






1) Accounting Operations (AP, AR, GL)




Oversee accounts payable and receivable processes to ensure timely and accurate processing of payments, receipts, and allocations.


Ensure customer and vendor reconciliations are performed and reviewed, including monitoring of aging reports and follow-up actions.


Maintain accurate general ledger postings and ensure proper supporting documentation for all transactions.


Manage month-end close activities, including review of journals, accruals, prepayments, and account reconciliations.




2) Retail Accounting and POS Control




Ensure monthly billing and retail sales reporting is complete and accurate.


Reconcile point-of-sale (POS) data to accounting records and investigate variances with Retail Operations.


Monitor inventory accounting movements and support inventory turnover reporting and reconciliation.




3) Financial Reporting (Preparation and Accuracy)




Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements in line with IFRS/GAAP and company policies.


Prepare monthly management reports, including P&L statements and key supporting schedules for review by the CFO/Financial Controller.


Ensure financial reports are complete, accurate, and supported by reconciliation schedules before submission for internal review.




4) Operational Financial Controls (Monitor and Escalate)




Implement and enforce accounting policies and procedures to safeguard assets and maintain financial integrity.


Ensure segregation of duties is applied within AP, AR, cash handling, POS processes, and journal approvals.


Review high-risk areas and exception items, including manual journal entries, credit notes, write-offs, adjustments, refunds, and unusual vendor/customer activity.


Perform variance and exception reviews (e.g., unusual movements, out-of-pattern transactions, repeated overrides) and document findings.


Escalate suspicious transactions, control breaches, or significant variances to the CFO/Financial Controller and support follow-up actions.


Support Internal Audit by providing documents, explanations, and evidence of control performance (without compromising audit independence).




5) Tax and Statutory Compliance




Ensure compliance with tax regulations, including preparation and filing of corporate tax returns, VAT/GST, and payroll-related taxes where applicable.


Maintain accurate tax working papers and coordinate with tax consultants and authorities as required.


Ensure adherence to applicable IAS and local regulatory requirements.




6) Audit Coordination and Close-Out




Serve as the main contact for external auditors for accounting matters.


Prepare audit schedules and provide supporting documents and explanations in a timely manner.


Track audit findings and implement agreed corrective actions within Finance to strengthen controls and improve compliance.




7) Systems, Process Improvement, and Data Integrity




Ensure accounting systems and processes are optimised for accuracy, efficiency, and proper access control.


Work with IT and relevant departments to improve integration between ERP/accounting systems and other platforms (including POS).


Maintain proper master data controls (customers, vendors, chart of accounts) and data integrity within systems.




8) Team Leadership and Capability Building




Lead and develop the accounting team to ensure effective delivery of daily operations and month-end close.


Assign responsibilities, monitor performance, and ensure staff follow SOPs and control procedures.


Conduct performance reviews and provide coaching and training to improve skills and compliance.


Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, and professionalism within the department.




Job Requirements








CPA or ACCA or equivalent professional accounting certification (required).


Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field (required).


Minimum 10 years of accounting experience, with at least 2 years in a supervisory or management role.


Proven experience managing AP, AR, general ledger, and month-end close.


Experience supporting retail accounting operations, including POS reconciliations and P&L reporting.


Experience supporting audits and implementing corrective actions from findings.


Strong knowledge of IFRS/GAAP, tax regulations, and audit requirements.


Proficiency with accounting software and ERP systems; familiarity with retail POS systems.


Strong skills in reconciliations, reporting, and operational control monitoring.


High attention to detail and strong quality control habits.


Strong leadership and team management capability.


Strong analytical skills with ability to identify exceptions and control issues.


Clear communication skills and ability to escalate issues with evidence and recommendations.


Strong organisation and ability to manage deadlines and multiple priorities.




 












 
To Apply
To apply for this job simply click on the blue "Apply" button below.  If you prefer to use email instead, please send your CV and other relevant documentation to 
[email protected]
.  Please include the Job ID "
#29162
" in the email's subject to ensure your application is processed.





            

        
Apply

JOB SUMMARY


 




Sheraton Port Moresby Stanley Hotel and Suites is seeking an enthusiastic, service-focused, and results-driven 
Assistant Health Club Manager
 to support the leadership and daily operations of our Health Club and wellness facilities.






This exciting role is responsible for assisting in the management of the gymnasium, swimming pool, spa, sauna, steam rooms, locker facilities, and wellness programs while ensuring exceptional guest experiences, operational excellence, safety compliance, and team performance.




 


CANDIDATE PROFILE 


 


Education, Skills and Experience
 


• Diploma or Degree in Health Education, Recreation, Physical Education, Fitness, Wellness, or a related field.
• Minimum 2-3 years' supervisory or management experience within a hotel health club, fitness centre, wellness facility, spa, or recreation environment.
• Strong understanding of fitness, wellness, recreation, and luxury guest service operations.
• Experience with budgeting, rostering, workforce planning, and operational reporting.
• Current CPR, First Aid, and Pool Safety/Lifeguard certification preferred.
• Proven leadership, coaching, communication, and relationship-building skills
• Ability to work flexible schedules, including weekends, public holidays, and shifts.
• Strong organizational skills and commitment to delivering exceptional guest experiences.
 


 


CORE WORK ACTIVITIES


 


Managing Health Club and Operations

• Schedules events, programs, and activities, as well as the work of others.
• Develops and implements menu of classes and services, including special programs.

Stock Controller


Royal Papua Yacht Club
Location:
 Port Moresby, National Capital District
Department:

Main Objective


The Stock Controller examines and analyses stock records to determine the club's stock status and prepares financial reports concerning operating procedures.

Collect and analyse data to detect deficient controls, duplicated effort, extravagance, fraud, or non-compliance with club rules, regulations and management policies.

RPYC recognises that injury and illness are preventable. All incidents and injuries must be reported to the Manager, no matter how minor.


Employees must comply with all relevant Acts, regulations and club safety rules, policies and procedures, and correctly wear all protective equipment supplied during work hours or in specifically designated areas.


Competencies




Dependability:
 Reliable, responsible and able to fulfil obligations.

 Able to accept criticism and deal calmly and effectively with high-stress situations.


Leadership:
 Willing to lead, take charge, and offer opinions and direction.

29153.description:
Summary






This position is responsible for managing the financial and contractual aspects of construction projects from planning to final handover. The role involves detailed cost estimation, tender preparation, contract administration, and project closeout, ensuring value for money and compliance at every stage.


Duties and Responsibilities






1. Pre-Construction Stage (Planning, Cost Estimation, and Contract Preparation)




Prepare feasibility studies and cost plans to assess project viability.


Develop preliminary and detailed cost estimates, covering material, labour, and associated costs.


Review drawings, Bills of Quantities (BOQ), Bills of Materials (BOM), take-offs and specifications.


Review design development and advise management on cost impact.


Support value engineering and recommend cost effective solutinos. 


Prepare and review tender documents and scope of works.


Evaluate contractor tenders/bids and prepare comparison and recommendations.


Negotiate prices and commercial terms with contractors and suppliers.


Propose cost-saving strategies and implement value engineering initiatives.


Ensure adherence to local regulations, statutory requirements, and internal standards.




2. Construction Stage (Contract Administration, Cost Control, and Monitoring)




Review and assess progressive claims, variations, and change orders.


Perform on-site inspections and quantity validations of completed works.


Prepare and issue interim payment certificates on a regular basis.


Coordinate with Project Manager, consultants, contractors and procurement team on commercial matters.


Manage disputes and contractual communication with external parties.


Monitor project cost against approved budget and identify possible cost overruns.




3. Post-Construction (Final Accounts and Closure)




Compile final accounts and close-out costs for each project.


Approve final subcontractor and supplier claims.


Ensure retention release and processing of all contractually required deductions.




4. Completion & Handover




Support final project handover activities and checklist completion.


Ensure receipt of all warranty documents, maintenance manuals, and as-built records.


Facilitate final regulatory approvals and statutory compliance certifications.




Job Requirements








Degree in Quantity Surveying, Civil Engineering, or Construction Management.


5–10 years’ experience in project cost control and contract administration.


Proficiency in tendering, cost planning, and post-contract activities.


Skilled in contract negotiation and commercial risk management.


Experience with construction measurement and cost software.


Strong leadership and team coordination capabilities.


Ability to manage multiple tasks under tight deadlines.


Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.

1. Culinary Leadership & Menu Development




Design, execute, and continuously improve cuisine menus
.


Develop seasonal specials, tasting and event catering menus aligned with current market trends and target demographics.


Create standardized recipe cards including precise ingredient weights, yield calculations, portion control guidelines, and step-by-step plating guides.


Ensure food quality, presentation standards, and flavor profiles remain consistently high during all service periods.




2. Kitchen Operations & Service Management




Oversee daily station setups (mise en place), service workflow, line management, and breakdown procedures.


Expedite orders during peak service hours to maintain fast ticket times, smooth communication with Front of House (FOH), and low table wait times.


Monitor inventory shelf-life rotation (FIFO) and daily prep lists to minimize waste and stockouts.


Oversee station equipment maintenance, ensuring routine checks, cleaning schedules, and repair logging are maintained.




3. Financial Management & Cost Control




Manage the kitchen budget to meet targeted food cost and labour cost percentage goals.


Manage inventory level by conducting weekly stock takes and implement corrective actions for stock losses or yield drops.


Monitor kitchen utility usage, operational supplies, and equipment lifespan to manage overhead expenses.




4. Team Leadership & Training




Conduct regular culinary skills training, knife skills workshops, food safety refreshers, and station cross-training.


Build weekly rosters based on sales forecasts, customer traffic trends, and labor budget constraints.


Foster a positive, respectful, and high-energy kitchen culture while resolving interpersonal conflicts and enforcing company policies.




5. Food Safety, Hygiene & Sanitation




Enforce total compliance with public health regulations, HACCP, and ISO/Food Handling safety standards.


Establish daily cleaning checklists, deep-cleaning routines, and hygiene audits for all preparation lines and storage areas.


Monitor cold-chain storage temperatures, walk-in chillers, freezer logs, and label/date systems for all raw and cooked inventory.


Ensure all back-of-house staff strictly adhere to personal grooming, uniform cleanliness, and hand-washing rules.








Job Requirements




Required Qualifications & Experience




Education:
 Diploma or Degree in Culinary Arts, Hospitality Management, or equivalent professional chef certifications.


Experience:
 Minimum 
5–7 years
 of culinary experience in high-volume Western restaurant   with at least 
2–3 years 
 in a Head Chef, Executive Sous Chef position.


Certifications:
 Valid Food Handler Certificate and Advanced HACCP / SERV Safe Manager certification.




Key Competencies & Technical Skills




Menu Engineering & Costing:
 In-depth understanding of food cost mechanics, recipe costing spreadsheets, and yield management.


POS & Kitchen Software:
 Hands-on experience with POS inventory modules, kitchen management software, and digital ticketing systems (KDS).


Leadership Under Pressure:
 Proven ability to stay calm, focused, and organized in high-stress, high-volume kitchen environments.


Communication:
 Excellent verbal and written communication skills to articulate dish concepts to FOH and delegate clearly to kitchen teams.




Work Environment & Physical Requirements




Ability to stand, walk, bend, and lift up to 25 kg (55 lbs.) throughout long shifts.


Flexibility to work nights, weekends, split shifts, and public holidays as required by restaurant operations.


Comfort working in environments with high heat, open flames, steam, and cold storage areas.

Hours & Overtime as per PNG law.

Summary






The Heavy Equipment Electrician is responsible for electrical troubleshooting, repairs, and preventive maintenance on heavy machinery such as excavators, trucks, generators, and loaders. The role covers PMS checks, diagnostics, and replacement of electrical components while ensuring all work is done safely and on schedule. The electrician also supports mechanics during servicing and assists with general workshop tasks when required. The position reports to the Workshop Supervisor or Fleet Maintenance Manager.


Duties and Responsibilities






Key Responsibilities


 


- Inspect, diagnose, troubleshoot, repair, and maintain electrical and electronic systems on heavy equipment.


- Perform electrical fault finding using diagnostic tools, wiring diagrams, schematics, and manufacturer manuals.


- Repair and replace wiring harnesses, batteries, alternators, starters, sensors, switches, relays, lighting systems, and other electrical components.


- Diagnose faults in electronic control systems, including engine and equipment monitoring systems.


- Conduct preventive maintenance and scheduled inspections to ensure equipment reliability and safety.


- Demonstrate sound knowledge of hydraulic systems to assist in diagnosing and identifying equipment faults.


- Apply strong understanding of mechanical systems, including components and their operation.


- Possess working knowledge of diesel engines and transmission systems to support effective troubleshooting and repairs.


- Work closely with mechanical technicians and other maintenance personnel to resolve complex equipment issues.


- Read and interpret electrical, hydraulic, and mechanical schematics and technical manuals.


- Ensure all repairs and maintenance activities comply with company procedures, safety standards, and manufacturer specifications.


- Maintain accurate records of inspections, repairs, parts used, and maintenance activities.


- Identify potential equipment failures and recommend corrective actions.


- Maintain a clean, safe, and organized work area.


Key Competencies


 


- Electrical troubleshooting and fault diagnosis


- Heavy equipment maintenance and repair


- Hydraulic system knowledge


- Mechanical system knowledge


- Engine and transmission knowledge


- Diagnostic equipment operation


- Technical documentation interpretation


- Problem-solving and attention to detail


- Teamwork and communication


- Safety awareness and compliance


Job Requirements






Qualifications and Requirements


 


- Trade qualification or technical certification in Automotive Electrical, Heavy Equipment Electrical, or a related field.


- Proven experience as a Heavy Equipment Electrician, preferably working with mining, construction, or industrial equipment.


- Strong knowledge of heavy equipment electrical and electronic systems.


- Sound knowledge of hydraulic systems and their basic operation and troubleshooting principles.


- Sound knowledge of mechanical systems and components.


- Good working knowledge of diesel engines and transmission systems.


- Ability to diagnose electrical and electronic faults using appropriate diagnostic equipment.


- Ability to read and interpret electrical wiring diagrams, schematics, and technical documentation.


- Experience working with heavy machinery such as excavators, bulldozers, loaders, dump trucks, graders, and other earthmoving equipment is preferred.


- Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.


- Ability to work independently and as part of a maintenance team.


- Good communication and reporting skills.


- Commitment to workplace health, safety, and environmental standards.

29145.description:
Workplace Type: Onsite 


Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.


 


Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.


 


We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.


 








Your Impact






As Shutdown Superintendent, reporting to the Maintenance Manager, you will lead the onsite Fixed Plant Shutdown team to safely deliver maintenance shutdown activities across Lihir's processing assets. This is a critical leadership role focused on driving operational excellence, ensuring shutdowns are executed safely and efficiently, and continuously improving shutdown strategies, processes, and performance.
You will be responsible for fostering a strong safety culture, leading high-performing teams, managing contractors and stakeholders, and ensuring shutdown execution delivers maximum value to the operation while maintaining compliance with all statutory and legislative requirements.










As part of our team, you will






 




Lead the execution of Fixed Plant shutdowns.


Manage shutdown resources, contractors, schedules, and budgets.


Drive safety, compliance, and operational excellence.


Champion shutdown management best practice and continuous improvement.


Partner with Operations, Maintenance, Supply Chain, and Reliability teams to deliver optimal outcomes.


Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing shutdown team.












Prerequisites for your success in this role






 




Relevant Trade Qualification or Degree.


Experience leading shutdowns within mining, processing, or heavy industry.


Strong knowledge of maintenance planning, scheduling, and shutdown management.


Demonstrated contractor management experience.


Proven ability to lead and develop high-performing teams.


Strong communication, stakeholder engagement, and problem-solving skills.


Experience with SAP or similar maintenance management systems preferred.


Commitment to safety, operational discipline, and continuous improvement.












Your work environment






This role is offered on a 21:21 FIFO roster flying from approved points of Australia throughout Australia and PNG.
Beyond work, you’ll enjoy the best of tropical island living, with access to a vibrant range of social and recreational activities. Our comprehensive relocation program ensures a smooth transition into the local community, including cultural orientation, international-standard schooling, quality healthcare services, and household support.










About Newmont




 








At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.​






Learn more about our purpose and values: 
About Newmont
​
Hear from our people: 
Life at Newmont
​






Important: Newmont does not ask candidates to pay money or share sensitive personal data outside our secure application process. If this happens, please report it to our Business Integrity team: 
[email protected]
.







    	        
Apply

PNG MOTORS | PORT MORESBY


SCAN CLERK


Every document counts. Every detail matters.


We're looking for someone who believes there's a place for everything and everything should be in its place. If you're organised, detail-focused and the kind of person who notices when something is missing, you might be exactly who we're looking for.


As our Scan Clerk, you'll help keep the information behind our business organised, accurate and easy to access. You'll be responsible for scanning, sorting and electronically filing company documents, checking records for completeness and maintaining digital and physical filing systems. You'll also assist with data entry, document retrieval and general administrative duties to ensure important information is properly recorded and readily available when needed.


This is a role where the small details make a big difference. A missing page, an incorrectly labelled file or a document saved in the wrong place can create unnecessary problems. We're looking for someone who understands the importance of doing things properly the first time.


You'll need good computer skills, confidence working with electronic documents and filing systems, and strong organisational abilities. Previous clerical, scanning, data entry or administrative experience would be an advantage, but a willingness to learn and a commitment to accuracy are just as important.


We're after someone reliable, patient and methodical who can manage repetitive tasks without losing focus, meet deadlines and handle confidential company information professionally. If you can stay organised when the paperwork starts piling up, you'll fit right in.


At PNG Motors, you'll be joining an established automotive business where every department plays a part in keeping things moving, including the people working behind the scenes.


THINK YOU'RE THE RIGHT FIT?


If you like keeping things organised, take pride in getting the little details right and believe every job is worth doing properly, we'd like to hear from you.


Send your CV and a brief cover letter to:

Coastal Retail Services Limited (CRSL) is seeking a qualified and experienced HACCP & Food Safety Specialist to join our team. The successful candidate will play a key role in promoting and maintaining Health, Safety, Security, and Environmental (HSSE) standards across our operations, with a strong focus on food safety and HACCP implementation within our catering services.


This position offers an exciting opportunity for a motivated professional to develop, implement, and maintain a comprehensive HACCP-based food safety management system while supporting CRSL's commitment to operational excellence and compliance.


HSSE Officer (HACCP & Food Safety Specialist) – x1


Location: Lae, Morobe


Application Code: AGL-HSSE-02


Requirements




Diploma or Degree in Occupational Health & Safety, Environmental Management, Food Science, Public Health, or related discipline.


Formal HACCP certification and demonstrated practical experience in HACCP implementation and management.


Minimum of 3–5 years' experience in HSSE, food safety, catering, hospitality, or related industries.


Strong knowledge of food safety regulations, hygiene standards, and risk management practices.


Experience conducting audits, inspections, and incident investigations.


Excellent communication, training, and report writing skills.


Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.


Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.




Key Competencies


The ideal candidate will demonstrate the ability to:




Develop, implement, and maintain HSSE policies, procedures, and programs across CRSL operations.


Lead the development and implementation of a HACCP (Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points) system for CRSL's catering and food service operations.


Conduct food safety risk assessments, audits, inspections, and compliance reviews.


Ensure compliance with applicable food safety regulations, industry standards, and company requirements.

HR EMPLOYEE RELATIONS MANAGER – MINING
 
 
 
 
Location: Papua New Guinea | Site-Based Position
   
 
An exciting opportunity for an experienced Employee Relations professional to take on a key leadership role within a mining operation in Papua New Guinea.
   
 Global Talent Search is seeking a capable, hands-on 
Employee Relations Manager
 to join an established mining operation in Papua New Guinea.
 This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced HR/IR professional who enjoys working in an operational environment, building relationships across diverse workforces and providing practical solutions to complex employee relations matters.
   
 Reporting to senior HR leadership, the successful candidate will be the primary HR representative on site, working closely with operational management, supervisors and employees to promote positive workplace relations, ensure compliance with employment legislation and support effective people management practices.
 The position requires a proactive, approachable and commercially minded professional who is comfortable working independently and managing employee relations matters at all levels.
 
 
 
 
Key Responsibilities
 
 
Lead employee and industrial relations activities across the operation, ensuring fair and consistent application of employment policies and procedures.
 
Manage workplace grievances, disciplinary matters, investigations, employee misconduct and performance management processes.
 
Provide practical advice and coaching to operational managers and supervisors on employee relations, performance management and employment legislation.
 
Develop and maintain positive working relationships with employees, employee representatives, contractors and other stakeholders.
 
Identify and proactively manage potential employee relations and industrial relations risks.
 
Support compliance with PNG employment legislation, regulatory requirements and company policies.
 
Oversee and support site-level HR administration, payroll coordination and workforce reporting.
 
Contribute to the ongoing improvement of HR policies, procedures and employee engagement initiatives.
 
Support broader HR activities, including recruitment, onboarding, workforce planning and employee development.
 
 
 
 
 
About You
 We are seeking an experienced Employee Relations professional with a strong operational focus and the confidence to manage challenging workplace matters in a remote environment.
 
Ideally, you will bring:
 
 
At least 5 years' experience in employee relations, industrial relations or HR management, with 10+ years highly regarded.
 
Demonstrated experience managing workplace investigations, grievances, disciplinary processes and performance management matters.
 
Strong knowledge of employment legislation, industrial relations frameworks and HR best practices.
 
Experience working within mining, resources, construction or other complex industrial environments.
 
Previous experience working in remote site operations will be highly regarded.
 
Excellent communication, stakeholder engagement, negotiation and conflict resolution skills.
 
The ability to work independently, exercise sound judgement and build credibility with operational leaders and employees.
 
Relevant tertiary qualifications in Human Resources, Industrial Relations, Law or a related discipline would be advantageous.
 
 Above all, we are looking for a 
practical, resilient and solutions-focused professional
 who enjoys being visible across the operation and is equally comfortable engaging with frontline employees and senior management.
 
 
 
 
The Opportunity
 This position offers the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to workforce stability, employee engagement and the continued development of effective people management practices within a mining environment.
 The successful candidate will join a professional HR function and play an important role in supporting operational leadership, strengthening employee relations and contributing to broader workforce initiatives.
 
 
 
 
To Apply
 If you are an experienced Employee Relations or Industrial Relations professional seeking a challenging and rewarding opportunity, we encourage you to apply.
 For a confidential discussion, contact 
Global Talent Search
, or submit your application and updated CV for consideration.





    	        
Apply

Credit Corporation PNG is recruiting a suitable candidate for the role of 
Finance Officer.


The Finance Officer is responsible for supporting Finance Operations through accurate and timely procurement and accounts payable processing, including purchase requisitions, purchase order receipting, invoice posting, supplier payment processing, supplier reconciliations, reporting, and audit ready documentation. The role ensures compliance with procurement, accounts payable, approvals, risk and quality requirements, while providing reliable support to business units, suppliers and internal stakeholders. 


Key Responsibilities:




Raise purchase orders and process purchase requisitions within required timeframes, ensuring approvals and supporting documentation are complete.


Complete purchase order receipting within 24 hours of invoice receipt or delivery confirmation, with complete documentation and approvals.


Prepare purchase order reports and analysis, including follow-up with business units and suppliers to obtain statements of account, invoices and supporting information.


Post invoices accurately and on time, including staff rentals, staff salary sacrifice, regular monthly bills, office rental, PUDO services, office security, non-PO invoices, sponsorship and marketing invoices.


Process ad hoc payments, including sales incentives, employee final entitlement payouts and approved one-off payments to unregistered suppliers.


Create payments in Oracle after funds are transferred, load payments on CBXC and ensure payments are processed in line with payment cycles and approval requirements.


Update supplier summaries, supplier reconciliations and related payment records, ensuring unreconciled items older than 30days are identified, followed up and escalated.


Create remittance advice files in Oracle and distribute them to suppliers in a timely and accurate manner.


Support CVC reconciliation and Fin Connect postings when required.


Maintain soft-copy records in SharePoint and ensure AP, procurement, supplier, contract and travel records ate complete, accurate, compliant and audit ready.


Review suppliers, contracts and travel plans for potential financial, legal and operational risks, and escalate unresolved risk issues with 48 hours.


Submit required weekly and monthly procurement, accounts payable, reporting and documentation updates to the Manager Finance Operations & Accounting.


Support Finance Operations improvement initiatives, testing requirements and continuous improvement activities as allocated.




 


Key Performance Indicators:




Process purchase requisitions within 24-48 hours.


Issue purchase orders with 48 hours of approval.


Complete 100% purchase order receipting within 24 hours of invoice receipt or delivery confirmation.


Post non-PO matched invoices within three days with at least 98% accuracy.


Process 95% of approved supplier payments within agreed payments cycles.


Submit 100% of weekly and monthly procurement and accounts payable reports on time.


Maintain complete with zero missing documents and zero audit exceptions.


Resolve supplier and internal stakeholder queries within 48 hours, with zero overdue supplier queries.


Ensure zero policy breaches and 100% compliance with procurement, accounts payable, approval and risk requirements.


Complete all mandatory training and required learning hours.




 


Requirements & Qualifications:




Degree or Diploma in Accounting, Finance, Business or a related discipline from a recognised tertiary institution.


Relevant experience in accounts payable, procurement, finance operations or accounting support, preferably within financial services or a corporate environment.


Experience using computerized financial accounting systems, Oracle, payment platforms, spreadsheets, and document management tools.


Good working knowledge of procurement, invoice processing, purchase order receipting, supplier reconciliations and payment processes.


Strong attention to detail, accuracy, record keeping and compliance discipline.


Ability to work with business units, suppliers and internal stakeholders in a professional and timely manner.




 


Required Skills and Competencies:




Accounts payable and procurement processing.


Invoice verification, payment preparation and supplier reconciliation.


Financial systems, Oracle processing and CBXC payment loading.


Data analysis, reporting and spreadsheet skills.


Document control, SharePoint filing and audit-ready record management.


Risk awareness, escalation and compliance with approval limits.


Stakeholder communication, supplier follow-up and query resolution.


Time management, prioritization and ability to meet processing deadlines.




 


Values, Behaviour and Compliance Expectations:




Demonstrate CreditBank values and expected performance management behaviours through timely one-on-ones, performance reviews, development planning and learning participation.


Complete all mandatory training, Wednesday learning sessions and required learning hours.


Support staff engagement, psychological safety and business unit community or social development initiatives where required.


Maintain a customer and supplier service mindset, aiming for zero complaints and timely resolution of issues.


Take mandatory compliance leave as required and comply with all risk, quality, procurement, accounts payable and approval frameworks.


Identify, escalate and help mitigate financial, legal and operational risk early.




 


Other Duties:
