29076.description:
Ambitious – Persuasive – Technically Curious
Want to sell some of the biggest lifts in the Pacific? As a Key Account Manager (Junior or Key level) in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea, you sell Sarens crane rental and project services, including heavy lifting and engineered transport. You own a portfolio of customers, from the first lead and quotation to contract, handover and collection. You become the adviser customers trust, and you put Sarens in their project pipeline early. Safety stays at the centre of every deal you close.
Join the force behind #NOTHING TOO HEAVY, NOTHING TOO HIGH
Your job in a nutshell:




Sell crane rental and project services (heavy lifting and engineered transport) to new and existing customers, in line with the sales plan.


Own your customer portfolio from lead generation and quotation through to contract, handover and collection.


Build a strong pipeline and keep a Bid for Work funnel of at least three times your annual target.


Prepare clear quotations and tenders, and lead negotiations through to contract.


Work with Operations, Technical Solutions, Finance, HR and Legal to turn each offer into a safe, well-planned project.


Visit customer sites, build relationships with key decision makers, and share market insight with management.


Keep the CRM accurate and give a three-month rolling revenue forecast.


Report to the Depot Manager and work closely with Operations and Project Managers, the Technical Solutions and Proposals Team, and Finance.


Work in Port Moresby, with regular domestic travel and occasional overnight trips to customers, depots and project sites.




 


ABOUT YOU


You like a 
challenge
 and you like closing deals. You understand 
cranes and heavy transport
, or you're eager to learn fast. You listen to customers, spot what they need and build solutions around it. You negotiate firmly and keep the relationship strong. You work with 
high autonomy
, and you put 
safety first
 in every conversation, quote and site visit.
Required:

29073.description:
Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


In this role you will provide management and leadership within our mobile maintenance department. This rewarding role will see you provide daily mentoring, guidance, instruction, and training to the national workforce to increase safety performance, machinery uptime and efficient outcomes within a motivated and talented department.


Key Accountabilities




Coordinate workshop activities through the Mobile Maintenance Supervisors.


Give direction, delegate tasks and provide technical assistance to subordinates.


Liaise with senior maintenance leadership on planned maintenance.


Maintain stock levels and place orders as required.


Ensure cost control measures are considered by utilizing resources available to full capacity.


Report and rectify any hazardous sightings to the Mobile Maintenance Superintendent in the 800L workshop.


Ensure training requirements are met.


Organise and document weekly safety toolbox meetings workshop safety representatives.


Regularly monitors and evaluates staff performance in consultation with Mobile Maintenance Superintendent.


Provide coaching for performance improvement.


In conjunction with mobile maintenance superintendent, takes disciplinary action to address performance deficiencies, in accordance with the Company’s rules, policies and procedures.


Personally, responds to inquiries and complaints from the employees.


Responds to emergency situations as necessary.


Carry out other relative duties as directed by the Mobile Maintenance Superintendent.


Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.


Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.




About You 


Qualifications & Experience




Relevant trade qualification in Heavy Equipment Fitting, Auto Electrical and Automation. Minimum Certificate III required.


10+ years relevant work experience essential.


Underground mobile fleet such as Sandvik and Caterpillar and provide guidance of Methods, practices, techniques.


Ability to plan, assign, direct and coordinate a variety of functional specialties (areas) with overlapping work areas.


Must have at least 5 years in mobile fleet maintenance in a supervisory capacity. Should also have experience in training of both operating and maintenance personnel.


Experience in the use of Pronto will be advantageous.


Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.


Excellent trouble shooting skills.


Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.


Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.


Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.


Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.




Life at K92  


K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.


In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.


THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP 





    	        
Apply

29068.description:
Position NO.:
 EXHS.004




 ABOUT OPIC




The Oil Palm Industry Corporation (OPIC) is a state agency responsible for supporting and promoting the development of the oil palm industry in Papua New Guinea. OPIC works in partnership with oil palm growers, industry stakeholders, local communities, and relevant government agencies to promote a productive, sustainable, and environmentally responsible oil palm industry.


OPIC invites applications from suitably qualified, experienced, and motivated individuals for the position of 
Manager – Sustainability 
based at its Head Office in Port Moresby.


 




 PURPOSE OF THE POSITION




The Manager – Sustainability is responsible for leading and coordinating OPIC’s sustainability programs, projects, and community engagement initiatives. The position promotes environmentally responsible oil palm production, harmonious relationships with local communities, and the adoption of Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) standards and practices.


 


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES




The successful applicant will be responsible for:


Reviewing and analysing policies, procedures, and operational processes to identify improvements in sustainability, environmental management, RSPO standards, and community affairs.


Providing leadership, technical advice, direction, and support to OPIC project staff on sustainability and community-related matters.


Developing and delivering internal training and capacity-building programs to enhance staff knowledge and performance.


Leading the development and implementation of annual work plans and budgets in alignment with OPIC’s Corporate Plan, Vision, Mission, and Management Action Plan.


Monitoring and evaluating sustainability programs and projects to ensure that planned targets and objectives are achieved.


Coordinating with project staff and participating in management meetings, field days, seminars, demonstrations, and stakeholder conferences as required.


Preparing and submitting regular reports, recommendations, and progress updates to the General Secretary.


Building and maintaining effective relationships with oil palm growers, farming communities, oil palm companies, government agencies, development partners, and environmental organisations.


Representing OPIC in sustainability and community affairs engagements as delegated by the General Secretary.


Performing other relevant duties as directed by the General Secretary.




 


QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE




A bachelor’s degree in agriculture, Environmental Science, Economics, or another relevant discipline from a recognised university or tertiary institution.


At least five (5) years of relevant professional experience, preferably in a management or senior technical role within a large organisation.


A postgraduate qualification in a relevant field will be an advantage.


Experience in sustainability programs, environmental management, community development, stakeholder engagement, or RSPO standards and practices.


Demonstrated experience in strategic planning, budget preparation, work-plan implementation, monitoring, and evaluation.


Proven ability to lead teams, build staff capacity, and manage stakeholder relationships.




 


 KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS




Strong leadership, management, and decision-making skills.


Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.


Sound knowledge of strategic planning, policy analysis, development, and implementation.


Ability to lead change and manage teams with diverse skills and experience.


Strong stakeholder engagement, negotiation, and relationship-management skills.


Knowledge of environmental sustainability, community affairs, and sustainable palm oil production.


Familiarity with relevant Papua New Guinea legislation and policies, including the OPIC Act 1992, Public Services (Management) Act 1995, Public Finances (Management) Act 1995, applicable Public Service General Orders, and other relevant regulations.


 




REPORTING AND WORKING RELATIONSHIPS


The position reports directly to the General Secretary and works closely with OPIC Head Office management, project staff, and other relevant internal stakeholders.


The Manager will also engage with oil palm growers and farming communities, oil palm companies, the Conservation and Environment Protection Authority, the Department of Lands and Physical Planning, relevant government agencies, and other industry partners.


 


Interested applicants should submit the following documents:




A cover letter expressing interest in the position.


An updated Curriculum Vitae (CV).


Copies of relevant academic qualifications and professional certificates.


Contact details of at least three (3) professional referees, including the current or most recent supervisor.


Current Medical Certificate


Current Police Certificate




 


 APPLICATION SUBMISSION

Position Title: Parts Assistant


Location: Manus


Division: Carmedic


 


Overview


We are seeking a motivated, reliable, and customer-focused 
Parts Assistant
 to support the day-to-day operations in Manus. The successful candidate will assist with parts sales, inventory management, stock replenishment, and customer service while ensuring accurate record keeping and efficient departmental operations.


 


The role requires close collaboration with customers, suppliers, and internal departments to ensure parts availability, timely processing of orders, accurate inventory control, and the delivery of excellent customer service.


 


 


Key Responsibilities


Customer Service: Assist customers with parts enquiries, pricing, quotations, and product identification while maintaining high service standards.


Sales Support: Support parts sales activities by processing orders, preparing quotations, and assisting with customer transactions.


Inventory Management: Assist with receiving, storing, issuing, and replenishing stock while maintaining accurate inventory records.


Stock Control: Participate in stocktakes, cycle counts, and inventory reconciliations to ensure stock accuracy.


Procurement Support: Assist with the preparation and follow-up of purchase orders and supplier enquiries to ensure timely delivery of parts.


Record Keeping: Maintain organized and accurate records of inventory, sales transactions, deliveries, and customer information.


Administration: Provide administrative support relating to sales documentation, filing, reporting, and departmental operations.


Communication and Coordination: Liaise with customers, suppliers, and internal departments to ensure efficient processing of orders and resolution of enquiries.


Housekeeping and Safety: Maintain a clean, organized, and safe parts store and sales environment while ensuring compliance with Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) requirements.


Team Support: Provide assistance to the Parts Supervisor and other team members to achieve departmental objectives and service standards.


 


Qualifications


Certificate, Diploma, or Degree in Business Administration, Sales and Marketing, Supply Chain Management, Inventory Management, Automotive Parts Management, or a related field.


Minimum of 1-3 years' experience in parts sales, warehousing, inventory control, customer service, or a similar role.


Sound knowledge of Microsoft Office applications.


Experience with inventory management will be an advantage.


Basic understanding of inventory control, stock management, and customer service principles.


Good communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.


Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.


Must be conversant with Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) regulations.

The PNG Oil Palm Industry Corporation (OPIC) is a statutory organization mandated to support thesustainable development of the oil palm industry in Papua New Guinea.OPIC invites applications from suitably qualified and experienced professionals for the position of Internal Audit to support and lead the administration of strong financial governance, accountability, and transparency across the organization.


Role


OPIC invites applications from suitably qualified candidates for the position of Internal Audit Officer.


The role is responsible for conducting financial and accounting audits, ensuring compliance with financial regulations, and strengthening internal controls over OPIC’s accounting, payroll, and financial management systems


Key Responsibilities


The Account Internal Audit officer will be responsible for:


Conducting internal audits of financial statements, accounting records, and transactions Reviewing payroll, allowances, entitlements, and deductions for accuracy and compliance Auditing procurement, payments, revenue, and asset management processes


Assessing the effectiveness of financial controls, accounting systems, and procedures


Ensuring compliance with Public Financial Management Act, Public Finance regulations, OPIC policies, and accounting standards


Identifying financial risks, irregularities, and control weaknesses and recommending corrective actions Preparing audit reports with clear findings and recommendations for Management


Monitoring implementation of audit recommendations


Supporting fraud prevention and detection relating to financial and accounting activities Liaising with external auditors, finance officers, and management as required


Qualifications & Experience


Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance, or Auditing Professional qualification such as CPA will be an advantage


Minimum of 2–3 years’ experience in accounting, internal audit, or financial auditing


Strong knowledge of accounting standards, internal controls, payroll systems, and financial reporting Experience working in a statutory body, public sector, or large organization is an advantage


High level of integrity, analytical skills, and attention to detail Good report writing and communication skills

29057.description:
HOTEL MANAGER


Location: Southern Highlands | Papua New Guinea


An exciting opportunity to lead hotel operations in one of Papua New Guinea's most unique locations.


This is an excellent opportunity for a passionate hospitality professional to take ownership of a diverse hotel operation, drive service excellence and lead a dedicated team in a unique remote environment.


The successful candidate will be a confident, resourceful leader with strong operational expertise, commercial acumen and the ability to work independently while maintaining exceptional hospitality standards.


The Hotel Manager will oversee all aspects of daily hotel operations, including accommodation, food and beverage, housekeeping, maintenance, guest services and supporting facilities. You will be responsible for ensuring operational efficiency, financial performance, guest satisfaction and a safe, welcoming environment for guests and employees.


This is a hands-on leadership role suited to someone who enjoys taking initiative, solving challenges and making a tangible difference.


Key Responsibilities:




Hotel Operations:
 Oversee all daily operations, including accommodation, food and beverage, housekeeping, laundry, maintenance, recreation and transport.


Team Leadership:
 Lead, mentor and develop hotel employees, fostering a positive, accountable and high-performing team culture.


Financial Management
: Manage budgets, control operating costs and monitor key performance indicators to support profitability.


Guest Experience:
 Maintain high service standards, proactively manage guest satisfaction and resolve operational challenges.


Health, Safety & Compliance:
 Ensure compliance with HSE requirements, food safety, hygiene and essential utility standards.


Stakeholder Management:
 Build and maintain effective relationships with corporate clients, contractors, local authorities and other stakeholders.


Community Engagement:
 Develop strong relationships with local communities and suppliers.




About You:




A minimum of 5 years' experience in hotel management.


Proven experience managing multiple hotel departments and leading operational teams.


Strong financial management, budgeting and cost-control capabilities.


The ability to work autonomously and confidently in a remote location.


Excellent leadership, communication and problem-solving skills.


Proficiency in Property Management Systems (PMS), restaurant management and procurement software.


A hands-on, adaptable and solutions-focused approach.


Knowledge of HACCP and food safety standards, with relevant certifications highly regarded.


A valid driver's licence and the ability to pass a pre-employment medical.


A minimum of Year 12 education with extensive hotel management training.


Experience managing remote hotels, resorts, lodges or accommodation facilities supporting the resources sector will be highly regarded.




Why Consider This Opportunity?




Take ownership of a 60-room hotel in a unique location.


Enjoy a varied, hands-on leadership position with genuine responsibility.


Play a key role in developing a high-performing hospitality team.


Build relationships with local communities and corporate stakeholders.


Further develop your career in a challenging and rewarding hospitality environment.




Ready for Your Next Challenge? If you are an experienced hospitality professional who thrives on responsibility, enjoys leading teams and is ready to embrace a unique opportunity in Papua New Guinea's Southern Highlands, we would love to hear from you.


Applications are open to Papua New Guinean nationals.


Applications cannot be accepted via email, WhatsApp and LinkedIn Messenger. Kindly apply via the job link





    	        
Apply

29054.description:
Head of Corporate Banking


CEO - Port Moresby, NCD




 












Position Goal


The Head of Corporate Banking is responsible for leading and overseeing the Bank's Corporate Banking business to achieve sustainable growth, profitability, and superior customer outcomes. The role is accountable for developing and executing the Corporate Banking strategy, driving revenue growth, managing portfolio quality and risk, strengthening key client relationships, and ensuring the delivery of comprehensive banking solutions to corporate customers.


The incumbent will provide strategic leadership to the Corporate Banking team, ensure effective execution of business plans, and maintain a strong risk and compliance culture while supporting the Bank's overall growth objectives.




Key Result Areas


Relationship Management & Client Coverage




Build and maintain strong relationships with key corporate clients, industry leaders, business associations, and strategic stakeholders.


Lead the acquisition, retention, and development of large corporate and institutional banking relationships.


Oversee the delivery of integrated banking solutions, including:



Corporate lending and structured finance


Working capital facilities


Cash management


Ensure relationship managers maintain effective account plans and maximize cross-selling opportunities across all business lines.






Represent the Bank at key client meetings, industry forums, and business events.




Portfolio Management & Risk Oversight




Assume overall responsibility for the quality, performance, and risk profile of the Corporate Banking portfolio.


Monitor portfolio concentrations by customer, industry, sector, geography, and product.


Ensure lending activities comply with the Bank's credit policies, risk appetite, and regulatory requirements.


Lead early-warning monitoring processes to identify and address emerging credit risks.


Work closely with the (Credit) Risk team, Credit Committee, and Executive Committee to maintain portfolio quality and minimize credit losses.


Ensure robust credit assessment, structuring, approval, monitoring, and remediation processes are maintained.




Financial Management & Performance Monitoring




Monitor and manage Corporate Banking financial performance, including revenue, profitability, balance sheet growth, and cost management.


Review monthly management accounts and address significant variances against budget and business plans.


Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) for the Corporate Banking team.


Drive productivity improvements and optimize resource utilization across the division.


Ensure achievement of budgeted financial and business objectives.




Product Development & Innovation




Lead the development, enhancement, and rollout of innovative corporate banking products and solutions.


Work collaboratively with Treasury, Transaction Banking, Retail Banking, Digital Banking, and other business units to deliver customer-centric solutions.


Ensure products remain competitive and aligned to customer needs and market trends.


Drive digital transformation initiatives within Corporate Banking.




Governance, Compliance & Regulatory Management




Ensure compliance with all internal policies, regulatory requirements, prudential standards, and applicable banking legislation.


Maintain effective governance frameworks and strong internal controls within Corporate Banking.


Ensure timely and accurate responses to Internal Audit, External Audit, Compliance, and regulatory requests.


Oversee remediation of audit findings, compliance breaches, and control weaknesses.


Promote a strong culture of ethical conduct, governance, and regulatory compliance.




Leadership & People Management




Lead, coach, mentor, and develop a high-performing Corporate Banking team.


Build leadership capability within the department and support succession planning initiatives.


Conduct regular performance reviews and provide ongoing feedback and development opportunities.


Foster a collaborative, customer-focused, and results-oriented work environment.


Ensure staff capability aligns with current and future business requirements.




 


 


Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)




Corporate Banking revenue and profitability growth.


Portfolio growth and asset quality.


Non-performing loan (NPL) ratios.


Return on assets and return on risk-adjusted capital.


New corporate customer acquisition.


Customer satisfaction and retention.


Regulatory and compliance performance.


Team engagement and performance outcomes.




 


Qualifications and experience 




Bachelor's Degree in Finance, Banking, Economics, Business Administration, Commerce, or a related discipline.


Master's Degree (MBA) or postgraduate qualification in Finance, Economics, Banking, or related field is highly desirable.


Professional banking or risk management certifications will be an advantage.




Experience




Minimum 10-15 years' banking experience with significant exposure to Corporate Banking, Wholesale Banking, Institutional Banking, or Commercial Banking.


At least 5 years in a senior leadership or executive management role.


Demonstrated experience managing large corporate client portfolios and complex lending transactions.


Proven track record in business development, relationship management, and strategic execution.


Experience operating within regulated banking environments.




Technical Knowledge




Strong knowledge of:



Corporate and commercial lending


Credit analysis and portfolio management


Cash management and transaction banking


Risk management frameworks


Financial analysis and structuring


Banking regulations and compliance requirements






Sound understanding of financial markets and corporate banking trends.


Strong business planning and financial management capabilities.






Skills & Competencies




Strategic thinking and commercial acumen.


Exceptional leadership and people management skills.


Strong negotiation and influencing ability.


Excellent stakeholder management and relationship-building capability.


High-level communication and presentation skills.


Strong analytical and decision-making capability.


Risk-aware and governance-focused mindset.


Ability to drive change, innovation, and execution.


Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.




Culture Fit




Respect for PNG’s diverse cultures and communities.


Commitment to NBCL’s mission of operational excellence and customer service.


Willingness to support cross-functional teams and branch initiatives.













    	        
Apply

29053.description:
Network Engineer


Information Communications Technology - Port Moresby, NCD




 












Network Engineer


 


National Banking Corporation Limited (NBCL) is seeking a qualified and experienced Network Engineer to join our Information Technology team. This role is responsible for the implementation, administration, monitoring, maintenance, and support of the Bank’s network and telecommunications infrastructure, ensuring secure, reliable, and high-performing connectivity across the organization.


 


Reporting to the Network Manager, the successful candidate will support and manage enterprise network services, including Local Area Networks (LAN), Wide Area Networks (WAN), SD-WAN, wireless networks, internet connectivity, firewalls, Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), cloud networking, telecommunications services, and network security platforms.


The Network Engineer plays a critical role in maintaining the availability, reliability, performance, and security of the Bank’s network infrastructure across branches, data centres, cloud environments, and digital banking platforms. The role also contributes to infrastructure modernisation initiatives, continuous improvement, and operational excellence to support the Bank’s strategic objectives.


 


Key Responsibilities:




Implement, configure, maintain, and support enterprise network infrastructure and telecommunications systems.


Monitor network performance and proactively resolve connectivity, capacity, and security issues.


Administer and support LAN, WAN, SD-WAN, wireless, VPN, firewall, and cloud networking solutions.


Ensure network security controls are implemented and maintained in line with industry standards and organisational policies.


Provide technical support and troubleshooting for network-related incidents and service requests.


Support business continuity and disaster recovery requirements for network services.


Collaborate with vendors, service providers, and internal stakeholders to deliver reliable network services.


Contribute to network upgrades, infrastructure projects, and digital transformation initiatives.


Maintain accurate network documentation, configurations, and operational procedures.




This is an excellent opportunity for a motivated professional who is passionate about network technologies, cybersecurity, and delivering high-quality infrastructure solutions in a dynamic banking environment.











    	        
Apply
